MAC Filtering exploits the uniqueness of the MAC address of every network device to determine if the device can or cannot access your wireless network.

detailed_results.question: What is Access Control and how does it differ from MAC Filtering?
detailed_results.expected: Access Control is used to block or allow specific client devices to access your network (via wired or wireless) based on a list of blocked devices (Blacklist) or a list of allowed devices (Whitelist). MAC Filtering exploits the uniqueness of the MAC (Medium Access Control) address, a unique 12-digit hexadecimal address (for example, D8:5D:4C:B4:46:EA) of every network device, to determine if the device can or cannot access your wireless network.

detailed_results.question: How can you remotely access USB storage connected to the router?
detailed_results.expected: You can access your USB disk outside the local area network. For example: • Share photos and other large files with your friends without logging in to (and paying for) a photo-sharing site or email system. • Get a safe backup for the materials for a presentation. • Remove the files on your camera’s memory card from time to time during the journey.
detailed_results.generated:
1. Insert your USB storage device into the modem router’s USB port and wait until the USB LED is solid.  
2. From a computer outside your local network, open a web browser.  
3. In the address bar type ftp://<WAN IP address of the modem router>:<port number> or ftp://<domain name of the modem router>:<port number>.  
4. Press Enter to connect to the router’s FTP server and browse or download files.  
5. To upload files, open a third-party network-file-management app and connect to the same FTP address.
